claims.supporting_quote: loss-of-function mutations in three genes, namely KRIT1 (CCM1), CCM2 and PDCD10 (CCM3)
claims.text: Cerebral cavernous malformation is a cerebrovascular disease of genetic origin; its pathogenesis has been associated with loss-of-function mutations in three genes, namely KRIT1 (CCM1), CCM2 and PDCD10 (CCM3).

claims.supporting_quote: which are implicated in defense mechanisms against oxidative stress and inflammation
claims.text: The three CCM genes are implicated in defense mechanisms against oxidative stress and inflammation, which provides a pathway rationale for testing an agent directed at oxidative stress in this disease.

claims.supporting_quote: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to investigate the safety, efficacy and pharmacokinetics of REC-994 (200 mg and 400 mg) compared to placebo
claims.text: The SYCAMORE study (NCT05085561) is a two-part, multicentre Phase 2 study of REC-994 at 200 mg and 400 mg once daily compared with placebo in adults with symptomatic cerebral cavernous malformation; Part 1 runs for 12 months and Part 2 is an optional long-term part for eligible participants completing Part 1.

forbidden_terms: similar to what we might expect without any treatment
target: Superoxide-mediated oxidative stress in CCM (disease genes KRIT1/CCM1, CCM2, PDCD10/CCM3)
